name: grace_prevents_sensor_repause
description: After the door/window pause ends, the same sensor opens again inside Climate Advisor's own 90-min automation grace: since Issue #1142 the grace does NOT hold off the pause (rule 3), the reopen is paused at once

events.note: Hot day, cooling active (classifier.py derives cool for a hot day)
Hot outdoor — nat-vent not viable (above threshold)
Door opens again 1 minute after resume, well within the 90-min grace window — grace should block re-pause.
No-op re-assertion of the same readings so the scheduler advances past the 14:46 reopen and any (mis)pause actually lands.

assertions.reason: Sensor closes, automation resumes from pause

Issue #1142 (rule 3): the door opens again within Climate Advisor's own 90-min automation grace; that grace is not a manual override, so the open door is paused at once (outdoor 85F, nat-vent not viable). Previously 'resumed' (the grace held the pause).
Reopen inside the automation grace is paused: the AC is switched off for the open door (rule 3).
The pause for the reopen is recorded.

verdict.summary: An automation grace does not hold off the pause (rule 3): the reopened door is paused at once
verdict.observed_behavior: Door opens within the automation grace → paused at once
verdict.expected_behavior: Only an occupant's manual override may keep heat/cool running with a window open (rule 3); Climate Advisor's own grace does not

notes: Issue #1142 (owner-approved golden change): rule 3 -- the only exception to 'no heat/cool with a window open after the debounce' is the occupant's manual override. Climate Advisor's own automation grace is not one, so it no longer holds off the pause: a window open past the debounce inside it gets the same answer as outside a grace (start nat-vent if the nat-vent FSM allows it, otherwise pause). Superseded by this note: the 14:46/14:47 assertions below are now 'paused' with _paused_by_door true; the older notes describing the grace guard are historical.

Issue #476: migrated to use_coordinator=true, skip_startup_coalesce=true, evaluated for real. The scenario was missing the actual sensor re-open event the 14:46 assertion refers to — added it. automation_grace_seconds set explicitly to 5400 (90 min) to match the scenario's own stated intent ('90-min grace' in the description) — the harness default (automation_grace_seconds=300/5min, which is what the sensor-closed-resume path actually reads, not manual_grace_seconds) would have made the '90-min' claim inaccurate, though the specific 14:45->14:46 (1 min) assertion timing would have passed with either duration.

The 14:46 assertion was 'no_action' in the legacy-simulator version. outcomes.py's production_outcome_at() has no 'no_action' sentinel — corrected to 'resumed' (carried forward from 14:45), the correct way to assert 'no NEW decision fired' — same pattern as grace_full_lifecycle_sensor_still_open.json's 13:12 assertion.

This scenario exercises the same grace-blocks-reopen guard (automation.py:2137-2150) also covered by grace_full_lifecycle_sensor_still_open.json. The 14:47 no-op temp_update advances the scheduler past the 14:46 reopen so a (mis)pause would actually land, and the 14:47 assertions (resumed + _paused_by_door false) fail if the grace guard is removed.
